title: 2014 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: Rectangle \(ABCD\) has sides \(CD=3\) and \(DA=5.\) A circle of radius \(1\) is centered at \(A,\) a circle of radius \(2\) is centered at \(B,\) and a circle of radius \(3\) is centered at \(C.\) Which of the following is closest to the area of the region inside the rectangle but outside all three circles?

solutions.text:
The parts of the three circles inside the rectangle are quarter-circles with radii \(1\), \(2\), and \(3\). Their total area is \[\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\pi+\dfrac{9\pi}{4}=\dfrac{7\pi}{2}.\]

Using \(\pi\approx\dfrac{22}{7}\), this total is about \(11\). The rectangle has area \(3\cdot5=15\), so the desired area is about \(15-11=4\).

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Inside the rectangle, each circle contributes a quarter-circle sector.
Subtract the total sector area from the rectangle area and approximate \(\pi\).
